resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) / Certificate of Compliance
resale_co.issued_by: Zoning Officer / Code Enforcement Officer (Zoning and Code Enforcement)
resale_co.lead_time: No application can be filed without a settlement date. All fees must be paid before scheduling an inspection. The code says the certificate is issued (or the failures listed) within 10 business days after the written application.
requirements: Inspection for conformance with the Borough Zoning and Property Maintenance Ordinances (Section 262-4B)
Additions, attic or basement apartments, finished basements, garages, sheds, pools, second kitchens and decks must have had permits or a variance
Exterior graded for drainage; sidewalks (to the curb line), walkways and driveways in good repair; weeds and plant growth kept down
Separate Fire Department smoke detector / CO inspection is also needed to close
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the CCO application (needs a settlement date) and return it with payment (check or cash) to Zoning and Code Enforcement, 514 W. Atlantic Avenue, Haddon Heights. The applicant is responsible for scheduling all inspections and re-inspections after fees are paid.

evidence.quote: Per Ordinance 2018:1453, no residential properties may change ownership or tenancy until a Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO) is issued by the Zoning Officer and a Smoke Detector/Carbon Monoxide Inspection is also required by the Fire Department.
As per Ordinance 2018:1453 it is required to apply for and receive a Certificate of Compliance issued by the Code Enforcement Officer
Please be aware that this inspection is DIFFERENT from the inspection the Fire Department conducts. You will need BOTH certificates in order to close.
No residential premises may be changed in tenancy, use or ownership unless a certificate of continued occupancy has been issued by the Enforcement Officer.

evidence.quote: The owner/seller of the property is required to obtain the certificate of occupancy.
The Enforcement Officer shall, within 10 business days after receipt of a written application for a certificate of continued occupancy, either issue said certificate
Brian Kelly Zoning Official & Code Enforcement Officer

resale_co.notes: New this check: Borough Code Chapter 262 (Residential Certificate of Continued Occupancy, adopted 6-3-2020 by Ord. No. 1489, replacing the 2018 Ord. No. 1453 the web page and form still cite) was read through the ecode360 print view. It requires a certificate before any change of tenancy, use or ownership of one- or two-family homes, townhouses and condos, makes the owner/seller responsible, and exempts transfers between spouses, parent and child, or siblings. The code fees match the form ($11 filing, $50 inspection, one free follow-up, $25 each after); the code lets the officer waive the inspection fee if a certificate was issued within the last 90 days. If an inspection fails, the property may close and/or be occupied without the certificate once the purchaser's agreement is accepted by the Enforcement Officer, for no more than 90 days while violations are abated (Section 262-2.2). Zoning Official and Code Enforcement Officer: Brian Kelly, zoning@haddonhts.com, 856-547-7164 ext. 33 (the form and page also list 856-546-2580). Current form is DocumentCenter/View/3128 (January 2025). Rental property registration and lead paint inspections are separate rental programs.

requirements: One smoke detector on each level including basement and any attic reachable by stairs; each level of each unit in a two-family
Ceiling-mounted at least 4 inches from walls, at least 36 inches from cold air returns and bathroom doors, away from ceiling fans; wall-mounted 4 to 12 inches below ceiling
UL-approved CO detector in the vicinity of each sleeping area
House number visible from the street, Arabic numerals at least 3 inches
2-A:10-B:C extinguisher no more than 10 lbs, charged, in a conspicuous place no more than 10 feet from the kitchen, instructions visible (form still lists it)

fire_cert.notes: DCA LEA Registry (July 2026) lists Haddon Heights' fire code enforcing agency as 'F' (Fire Department), consistent with the Haddon Heights Fire Department Bureau of Fire Prevention. Fee sheet is from August 2022 (PDF metadata) and is still the form linked on the Fire Prevention page; the link now redirects to the same file with '?bidId=' added, which is the address cited here. New this check: Borough Code Section 233-7A(3) was read through ecode360. It lists the same $75 / $100 / $140 tiers and $35 reinspection, plus a $20 fee for a missed appointment and a $30 senior discount credited on the first inspection (both added above). The code table also has a first row of '$40' for resale smoke and CO inspections of one- and two-family homes, which the form does not show; it is not recorded as a fee and should be asked about. Section 382-6B says the first reinspection is free, while the form and the fee table charge $35. The CCO form gives the Fire Department number as 856-547-7164 ext. 80, while the fire form gives 856-546-7135 (ext. 81). No inspector email addresses are published on the page. The DCA fire directory lists Fire Official Benjamin Zwaska (bzwaska@haddonhts.com) and the smoke compliance office at Rear 608 Station Ave. The fire form still lists a 2-A:10-B:C extinguisher; the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), so confirm with the Bureau.
